claim: Census of simple rank-3 matroids on 8 elements; unique maximum T(2,0)=58 at U(3,8), runner-up 56; Fano deletion certificate.

correctness.evidence: Independent pair-mask dynamic programming counted 433,039 valid line families including the unique rank-2 family, hence 433,038 simple rank-3 labeled families. Mayhew-Royle Table 2 independently gives 68 simple rank-3 types on 8 elements. Direct subset expansion proves T_M(2,0)=58-sum_L(|L|-1)(|L|-2), hence unique maximum 58 and exact gap 2. Fano-line pair coverage was independently checked.

originality.evidence: The 68-type census is established by Blackburn-Crapo-Higgs and Mayhew-Royle. The T(2,0) maximum/gap is an immediate consequence of the defining Tutte subset expansion via the closed line-size formula, not a new census-dependent extremal phenomenon; the Fano-minor fact is classical.

value.evidence: After known census coverage and the elementary T(2,0) formula, the remainder is a finite catalogue annotation and a classical Fano example, with no new general theorem, representability classification, or algorithmic improvement.

independent_checks.fano_certificate: seven listed lines cover all 21 pairs exactly once after deleting point 4

literature.citation: D. Mayhew and G. F. Royle, Matroids with nine elements, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 98 (2008), 415-431; arXiv:math/0702316, Table 2.
literature.mapping: Complete catalogue; Table 2 gives 68 simple rank-3 matroids on 8 elements and states agreement with Blackburn-Crapo-Higgs.

repair.assessment: Can reframe as a catalogue annotation and replace exhaustive maximality by the direct line-size formula, but that does not restore sufficient originality/value.
